heading: Tennessee Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Tennessee paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Tennessee does not impose individual income tax on ordinary employment earnings, but federal payroll taxes and employee benefits still affect your net income.

Whether you work in Nashville, Memphis, Knoxville, Chattanooga or another Tennessee community, this calculator can help you compare employment opportunities and manage monthly expenses.

## How to Use the Tennessee Paycheck Calculator

Select annual salary or hourly wages and enter your gross compensation before taxes.

Choose your payment frequency. Enter the full federal income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include healthcare premiums, retirement contributions and other employee deductions.

Enter year-to-date taxable wages if you are approaching annual federal payroll contribution thresholds.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown and remaining take-home income.

Tennessee employees generally do not need a separate state personal income tax withholding certificate.

## Tennessee Payroll Taxes in 2026

Your actual paycheck depends on taxable earnings, federal withholding elections and employee benefits.

Visit the [Tennessee Department of Revenue](https://www.tn.gov/revenue.html) for official information about state taxation.

## Does Tennessee Have State Income Tax?

Tennessee does not impose individual income tax on ordinary wages.

Employees working and residing in Tennessee therefore generally do not have Tennessee personal income tax deducted from their regular paychecks.

However, this does not mean employment earnings are completely tax-free.

Federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other applicable deductions continue to reduce gross earnings.

Tennessee previously imposed the Hall Income Tax on certain interest and dividend income. This tax was repealed effective January 1, 2021.

The former Hall Income Tax should not be included in a 2026 paycheck calculation.

Read the official [Tennessee income tax withholding guidance](https://revenue.support.tn.gov/hc/en-us/articles/360057595051-GEN-34-Income-Tax-Withholding) for confirmation.

## Federal Income Tax on Tennessee Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on your taxable earnings, filing status, payment frequency and information supplied on Form W-4.

Employees with multiple jobs or additional household income may need different withholding adjustments.

Federal income tax uses progressive rates, meaning different portions of taxable income are subject to different percentages.

Employers calculate withholding using the procedures in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

The [IRS Form W-4 instructions](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-4) explain how employees can communicate their withholding elections.

You can also use the official [IRS Tax Withholding Estimator](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/tax-withholding-estimator) to evaluate whether your current deductions are appropriate.

## Social Security and Medicare Contributions

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered earnings toward Social Security.

The annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500 in 2026.

For example, an employee receiving $3,000 in covered wages before reaching the annual limit would contribute $186.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings.

A $3,000 Medicare-covered paycheck would produce a $43.50 deduction.

Employers generally collect an additional 0.9% once Medicare-covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review the [Social Security Administration wage base information](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html) and [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for official annual limits and contribution rules.

## Tennessee Paycheck Example: $78,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $78,000 annually before taxes.

Assume the employee is single, uses a modern federal Form W-4, has not selected the multiple-jobs checkbox and has no additional credits or withholding adjustments.

Also assume there are no employee benefit deductions or reached annual payroll contribution thresholds.

Your actual paycheck may differ depending on retirement contributions, insurance premiums and withholding elections.

## Tennessee Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can calculate gross earnings using regular working hours and qualifying overtime compensation.

Suppose you earn $25 per hour and work 40 regular hours plus eight qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$25 × 40 = $1,000.

Overtime earnings:

$25 × 1.5 × 8 = $300.

Total gross earnings: $1,300.

Assuming ordinary payroll contribution coverage, Social Security would be $80.60 and Medicare would be $18.85.

Federal income tax and other employee deductions would also apply.

Consult the [Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development](https://www.tn.gov/workforce.html) and [US Department of Labor overtime requirements](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for applicable eligibility rules.

## Tennessee Unemployment Insurance

Tennessee's unemployment insurance program is funded through applicable employer tax premiums.

Ordinary employer unemployment insurance contributions should not be subtracted from employee take-home pay.

Read the [Tennessee covered employment guidance](https://lwdsupport.tn.gov/hc/en-us/articles/26108109587987-How-do-I-determine-if-my-employment-qualifies-as-covered-employment) for information about insured employment.

Independent contractors may have different tax and benefit obligations from ordinary W-2 employees.

## Does Nashville Have a Local Income Tax?

Nashville and other Tennessee municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes.

However, state and local sales taxes, property taxes, housing expenses and transportation costs can influence household purchasing power.

When evaluating employment opportunities, compare net salary and expected living expenses separately.

Visit the [Tennessee sales and use tax resources](https://www.tn.gov/revenue/taxes/sales-and-use-tax.html) for information about consumption taxes.

## Working Across Tennessee State Borders

Tennessee borders several states that impose individual income tax.

Employees residing in Tennessee while working in Georgia, North Carolina or another income-taxing state may have additional withholding obligations.

Living in Tennessee does not automatically eliminate another state's income tax on qualifying employment earnings.

Remote work and employment across multiple jurisdictions may require additional income allocation calculations.

Consult your employer and relevant state tax authorities before applying a standard Tennessee-only paycheck estimate.

## Managing Your Tennessee Take-Home Income

Build your monthly budget around estimated net earnings rather than gross salary.

Account for housing, transportation, healthcare, groceries and required debt payments.

Traditional retirement contributions may reduce current federal income-taxable wages, while Roth contributions generally do not offer the same immediate reduction.

Review the [IRS retirement plan guidance](https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans) before changing your contributions.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) and [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help you establish realistic financial goals.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Tennessee deduct state income tax from wages?

No. Tennessee does not impose individual state income tax on ordinary employee wages. Federal taxes and other applicable deductions still apply.

### Does Tennessee still have the Hall Income Tax?

No. The former tax on qualifying interest and dividend income was repealed effective January 1, 2021.

### How much will I take home from a $78,000 salary in Tennessee?

Under the single-filer assumptions illustrated above, estimated biweekly take-home pay is $2,450.12. Your actual result depends on federal withholding and employee deductions.

## Calculate Your Tennessee Take-Home Pay
